content: Apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1 (ASK1), also referred to as mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase kinase 5 (MAP3K5), is a member of the MAP kinase kinase kinase family. It plays a critical role in the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway. ASK1 specifically activates c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinases in a manner that is independent of Raf proteins. This activation occurs in response to various cellular stresses, including oxidative stress, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and calcium influx. ASK1 has been implicated in the pathogenesis of several diseases, including cancer, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and neurodegenerative disorders. The MAP3K5 gene, which encodes ASK1, is located on chromosome 6 at the locus 6q22.33. The protein itself is composed of 1,374 amino acids and contains 11 kinase subdomains. Northern blot analysis has revealed that the MAP3K5 transcript is highly expressed in the human heart and pancreas. Under non-stress conditions, ASK1 exists in an oligomerized state, which is necessary for its activation. This oligomerization is mediated by its C-terminal coiled-coil domain (CCC). However, ASK1 remains inactive due to the inhibitory effects of reduced thioredoxin (Trx) and calciumand integrin-binding protein 1 (CIB1). Trx suppresses ASK1 kinase activity by directly binding to its N-terminal coiled-coil domain (NCC). The activation of ASK1 is regulated in a redox-sensitive manner by Trx and in a calcium-sensitive manner by CIB1. Both Trx and CIB1 compete with tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) receptor-associated factor 2 (TRAF2), which is an activator of ASK1. Upon activation, TRAF2 and TRAF6 are recruited to ASK1, forming a larger molecular complex. ASK1 then undergoes homo-oligomerization through both its CCC and NCC domains, leading to its full activation via autophosphorylation at threonine 845. ASK1 has been shown to interact with a variety of proteins, including: C-Raf, CDC25A, DAXX, DUSP19, EIF2AK2, GADD45B, HSPA1A, MAP2K6, MAP3K7, MAPK8IP3, PDCD6, PPP5C, RB1CC1, TRAF2, TRAF5, and TRAF6.
